fields.h1: Build a Safety Sign in Sheet Your Crew Signs on a Phone
fields.hero_description: Get a safety sign in sheet that saves each attendee's name and e-signature to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Phone Sign in Sheet Records
fields.features_subheading: Six jobs the sheet does that a clipboard leaves for someone to finish after the meeting.
fields.feature_1:
One question per screen

Each attendee opens the sheet on a phone and answers one question at a time: name, crew, then signature. Nobody waits in line for the clipboard before the talk starts.
fields.feature_2:
A signature beside every name

The sheet captures an e-signature from each attendee and files it with the printed name for that meeting. Nobody has to guess whose initials sit on a smudged paper line.
fields.feature_3:
The topic and trainer at the top

Whoever runs the meeting fills in the header once: topic, date, location, and who led it. Each attendee signs under that header, so every signature belongs to one meeting.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders for anyone who missed it

The sheet compares sign-ins with your roster and sends a Slack, email, or in-app reminder to each person who is missing. Unanswered reminders escalate to a supervisor.
fields.feature_5:
A year of meetings in one table

Every sign-in is saved as a row in a database you own, with no cap on responses. Last March's toolbox talk sits next to this week's, not in a binder in the site trailer.
fields.feature_6:
Attendance in your training records

The sheet connects to any tool with an API, such as an HR or learning system, and sends each record there. Training history updates without anyone retyping a paper sheet.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Crews Sign In, and What Follows
fields.tab_content_1:
Every one of the 14 crew members signs the talk

Foreman Teodor Lusk runs a toolbox talk on trench safety every Monday at Corrigan Ridge Builders. His 14 crew members sign in on their phones, each with an e-signature beside a printed name. The sheet saves the topic and the date, with Teodor as the person who led it.
fields.tab_content_2:
For each of the 3 who missed it, a makeup date

Halvard Packaging puts 25 forklift operators on the roster for its quarterly refresher meeting, and 22 sign in. The other 3 each get an email with the date of Thursday's makeup session. Until they sign in there, the roster marks them as missed.
fields.tab_content_3:
Floor by floor, 58 of 61 reach the assembly point

Lanecrest Medical Plaza runs a fire drill, and staff sign in on their phones when they reach the assembly point. Fire warden Anouk Brevik watches a live count climb to 58 of 61. The count by floor shows where the 3 missing people work: 1 on floor 2 and 2 on floor 3.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 36 scanned sheets, 4 go to a person to check

Ferro Valley Water District has 36 paper sign in sheets from last year's safety committee meetings. Each scan is read into the same fields as the phone form. On 4 sheets a name is read at low confidence, and safety coordinator Gideon Marsh checks those before they are saved.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Safety Sign in Sheet
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a safety sign in sheet that records each attendee and reminds anyone who missed it, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write the header for each meeting
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Match the record to the training
fields.howto_step_1_des: Put the topic, the date, the start time, the location, and the trainer's name at the top. Keep the topic to a few words that tell one meeting from the next, such as trench shoring rather than safety.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for a printed name, a crew or employer, and a signature. On a site shared by several contractors, the employer column shows which company each worker came with.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Check whether the training falls under a standard that names its own record, such as forklift operator training. Add a field for each item that standard lists.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List everyone expected at the meeting, grouped by crew or shift. With a roster behind it, the sheet can show who did not come as well as who did.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the header fields and the roster into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the sheet and the database behind it. A later change, such as a field for hard hat checks, is one more prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide whether missed attendees hear by email or Slack, and name the supervisor a reminder escalates to when nobody responds. Put the makeup session date in the reminder text.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run it at one real meeting
fields.howto_step_7_des: Use it at next Monday's talk alongside the paper sheet, then compare the two. Every name on the paper sheet should appear in the database with a signature.

faq_plan.q: What is a safety sign in sheet?
faq_plan.a: A safety sign in sheet is the attendance record for a safety meeting or training session. Each attendee prints a name and signs under a header that gives the topic, the date, and who led it. Afterward it shows who heard the talk and who did not.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a safety sign in sheet?
faq_plan.a: Decide what the header needs and what each attendee fills in, then describe both to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. It builds the sheet as a form, along with the database each sign-in is saved to. Run it at one meeting before you retire the paper version.

faq_plan.q: What should a safety meeting sign in sheet include?
faq_plan.a: Put the meeting topic, the date, the location, and the name of whoever led it at the top. Below that, give each attendee a line to print a name and sign, and leave space at the bottom for the trainer's signature. When the sheet is built on Emergent, each signature is captured as an e-signature and kept with the name it belongs to.

faq_plan.q: How do you use a construction safety meeting sign in sheet on a job site?
faq_plan.ref: construction safety meeting sign in sheet
faq_plan.a: Hand it out at the start of the toolbox talk and collect it before the crew goes back to work. Add a column for each worker's employer, since several subcontractors can share one site and one talk. To hear what the crew took from the talk, follow it with a training feedback form a few days later.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a new daily safety meeting sign in sheet every day?
faq_plan.ref: daily safety meeting sign in sheet
faq_plan.a: Yes. Start a new, dated sheet for each daily safety meeting, and keep one meeting to a page. Name the day's topic in a few words: the same crew may sign 5 times a week, and the topic is what tells those meetings apart. With no response caps on forms built on Emergent, a crew can sign in every morning for a year without filling one up.

faq_plan.q: What is a fire safety sign in sheet used for?
faq_plan.a: A fire safety sign in sheet records who attended fire safety training, or who reached the assembly point in a drill. Under OSHA's 1910.157, where the employer has provided portable fire extinguishers for employee use, it must provide education in the general principles of fire extinguisher use upon initial employment and at least annually thereafter.

faq_plan.q: Where can I get a free safety meeting sign in sheet?
faq_plan.ref: free safety meeting sign in sheet
faq_plan.a: You can build one free on Emergent, since the free tier covers building and publishing. Describe the header and the attendee row, then publish the sheet before the next meeting. For visitors signing in at a front desk rather than a meeting, a sign in form fits better.

faq_plan.q: Why do employers use an OSHA safety meeting sign in sheet?
faq_plan.ref: osha safety meeting sign in sheet
faq_plan.a: Employers use it to show who attended a meeting held to instruct workers on hazards, when it took place, and what it covered. On construction sites, OSHA's 1926.21(b)(2) says the employer shall instruct each employee in the recognition and avoidance of unsafe conditions. A signed sheet from each meeting shows who was present for that instruction.

faq_plan.q: What fields does an OSHA safety training sign in sheet need?
faq_plan.ref: osha safety training sign in sheet
faq_plan.a: Give it a topic, a date, the trainer, and each attendee's signature, then add any record the standard behind the training names. For forklift operators, OSHA's 1910.178 says the certification shall include the name of the operator, the date of the training, the date of the evaluation, and the identity of the person(s) performing the training or evaluation.

faq_plan.q: Who signs a safety committee sign in sheet?
faq_plan.a: Every committee member at the meeting signs it, along with any guests. List members by name with a present or absent mark, and note the items discussed. With a short, fixed roster, a member who misses two meetings in a row stands out. If contractor guests must be logged as they leave the site, pair the sheet with a sign out form.
